title: ServicesManifest
description: Extended services.json contract for stateful service hosting (spec 091). Additive over the 063 contract: a ServiceEntry with kind='generic' and no init renders identically to today.

services.description: Supportive services the project depends on. Service names must be unique.

cache_inputs.description: Project paths whose contents drive cache invalidation.

agent_version.description: Producer identifier; 'manual-override' for hand-authored score.json (trusted over LLM inference).

name.description: Logical service name; interpolated into shell identifiers and paths.

binary.description: Executable name or absolute path, PATH-resolvable inside the performer.

data_dir.description: Mutable service-state path; MUST resolve under a writable location ($XDG_RUNTIME_DIR), never the read-only cache mount.

start_args.description: Optional argv override for in-container launch; each element is shell-quoted.

kind.description: Selects the coordinare-owned init recipe, launch template and protocol-level readiness probe (issue 413 widened the set beyond postgres/redis). 'generic' = no coordinare recipe: the launch is the manifest's own start_args and readiness is its health_command (both REQUIRED in-container). NEW in 091, widened by 413.

health_command.description: Argv-style readiness probe for the service, exit 0 = ready. REQUIRED for an in-container generic service (issue 413); coordinare-owned kinds have protocol-level probes built in. NEW in 413.

init.description: First-run initialization parameters. Only valid for kinds that initialize (postgres). NEW in 091.

allOf.$comment: VR-2: init only valid for an initializing kind.
issue 413: an in-container generic service must carry its own launch + probe (no synthesised default).

ServiceInit.description: Init parameters only — never a recipe, never a literal secret.

databases.description: Databases created idempotently on first run, each create-if-missing.

password_env_var.description: Name of the env var holding the admin secret. The recipe reads ${VAR}; the secret value is NEVER stored here, in argv, or in logs.
